What is the primary purpose of Error-Correcting Code (ECC) memory in a computer system?
options: To increase the overall memory bandwidth of the system.
To compress data before storing it, thus increasing effective memory capacity.
To detect and correct single-bit memory errors, improving data integrity and system reliability.
To enable faster memory access by caching frequently used data.
To manage virtual memory pages and swap data between RAM and disk.
